## Course Overview

Linear algebraic groups are fundamental objects and tools in mathematics, with wide applications in number theory, representation theory, automorphic forms, and dynamical systems on homogeneous spaces. 

The goal of this course is to systematically develop the theory of linear algebraic groups, focusing on their structural properties, representations, and root-theoretic classifications, laying a solid foundation for research in arithmetic geometry, the Langlands program, and related areas.

---

## Syllabus & Lecture Schedule

The notes are organized according to the 7 main modules of the course:

### [Weeks 1–2] Linear Algebraic Groups: Foundations & Jordan Decomposition
- Affine varieties and the definition of linear algebraic groups
- Subgroups, homomorphisms, and canonical examples ($\mathrm{GL}_n$, $\mathrm{SL}_n$, $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, $\mathrm{SO}_n$)
- Jordan-Chevalley decomposition (additive and multiplicative) in $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ and in abstract linear algebraic groups

### [Weeks 3–4] Tannakian Formalism and Lie Algebras
- Group actions on affine coordinate algebras $\mathcal{O}(G)$ and locally finite representations
- Tannakian perspective: reconstructing an algebraic group from its representation category
- The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$ as invariant derivations
- The adjoint representation $\mathrm{Ad}: G \to \mathrm{GL}(\mathfrak{g})$

### [Week 5] Tori in Algebraic Groups
- Diagonalizable groups and Cartier duality
- Character lattice $X^*(T)$ and cocharacter lattice $X_*(T)$
- Algebraic tori (split vs. non-split)
- Rigidity of tori, centralizers, and normalizers

### [Week 6] Quotients of Algebraic Groups
- Actions on algebraic varieties, orbits, and stabilizers
- Chevalley's Theorem on constructing subgroups as stabilizers of lines
- Existence and geometric construction of homogeneous spaces and quotient varieties $G/H$

### [Weeks 7–8] Reductive Groups
- The radical $R(G)$ and the unipotent radical $R_u(G)$
- Definitions and characterizations of semisimple and reductive groups
- Action of maximal tori on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ and the root space decomposition
- Basic properties of roots and root systems

### [Weeks 10–11] Parabolic Subgroups of Reductive Groups
- The Borel Fixed-Point Theorem for complete varieties
- Maximal connected solvable subgroups (Borel subgroups $B$)
- The flag variety $G/B$ and its projectivity/completeness
- Parabolic subgroups: standard parabolic subgroups and their classification

### [Weeks 12–13] Various Decompositions of Reductive Groups
- The Bruhat decomposition: $G = \bigsqcup_{w \in W} B w B$
- Relative root systems and decompositions over non-algebraically closed fields
- Connections to the Iwasawa and Cartan decompositions in Lie groups and arithmetic groups
